features.name: Simulations Page
features.does: Lists every simulation run for the project. Runs start from the LiveKit CLI or CI and their results, transcripts and traces land here.
features.value: One place where product, QA and engineering see whether the agent still does its job after every change.
features.say: This is where every test run of your agent lands, whether someone ran it from a laptop or your CI pipeline ran it on a pull request.
features.ask: Today, how do you find out that a prompt change broke something your agent used to handle well?
use_cases: Comparing a rewrite against the old agent
features.limits: Runs are started from the CLI ('lk agent simulate'), not from a button in the dashboard. demo-tour currently has no runs.
features.ask_technical: Where would simulations run for you: on every PR in CI, nightly, or by hand before a release?

features.name: Auto-generated Scenarios
labels: Simulates 5 sessions with scenario tests unique to your agent
features.does: Reads the agent's prompts, tools and logic and generates realistic caller scenarios, including edge cases nobody wrote down, then runs them.
features.value: A pass rate on paths you never explored within minutes, without writing a single test or making a single call.
features.say: You don't have to write tests from scratch: one command reads your agent and invents the tricky callers for you, then tells you which ones it failed.
features.ask: What are the calls that worry you most, the ones you'd never think to test by hand?
use_cases: Bootstrapping a test suite for a new agent
features.limits: Uploads agent source to LiveKit Cloud for generation (CLI asks to confirm). Generated scenarios are a starting point to curate.
features.ask_technical: Would you seed scenarios from source with '-n', or check in a curated scenarios.yaml?

features.name: Scenarios (simulated user + judge)
features.does: Each scenario gives an LLM-driven simulated caller a persona and a goal; an LLM judge grades the whole conversation against freeform expectations and gives pass/fail with a reason.
features.value: Tests the outcome of the whole call, the way a real customer experiences it, not just single replies.
features.say: Each test is a pretend caller with a goal, like 'book a room then change the name', and a judge that checks whether your agent actually got them there.
features.ask: If you had to write down what a perfect call looks like for your top use case, what would the must-haves be?
features.limits: Judge verdicts depend on clearly written, outcome-shaped expectations; vague expectations grade inconsistently.
features.ask_technical: Do you need to grade final state too (e.g. the DB booking), via an on_simulation_end check?

features.name: Pass/Fail Verdicts with Reasons
features.does: Shows each scenario's verdict with the judge's explanation and the full simulated conversation.
features.value: Anyone can see what broke and why, in plain language, without listening to recordings.
features.say: Every test says pass or fail and explains why in plain English, and you can read the whole conversation behind it.
features.ask: Who on your side would review these results: engineers, QA, or the business owner of the call flow?
features.limits: Verdicts are LLM-judged; pair with final-state checks for hard guarantees.
features.ask_technical: Would a non-zero exit code from the CLI gating your merge be enough, or do you need a report artifact too?

features.name: Quality Scores
features.does: Scores each run on task completion, conciseness and conversation flow; audio runs add turn-taking and transcript accuracy.
features.value: A trend line for quality, not just a list of failures, so you can see if the agent is getting better or worse.
features.say: Beyond pass and fail you get scores for whether it finished the job, stayed concise and kept the conversation flowing.
features.ask: What one number would your leadership use to say the agent is good enough to take more calls?
features.limits: Turn-taking and transcript accuracy only exist for audio runs.
features.ask_technical: Which metrics would you track per release: task completion, p95 caller-heard latency, entity accuracy?

features.name: Issues Detected and Fix Prompts
labels: GIVE THIS TO YOUR CODING AGENT
features.does: Groups failures into named issues with the conversations that show them, a recommended action, and a ready-made prompt to hand to a coding agent.
features.value: Shortens the loop from 'something is wrong' to a concrete fix.
features.say: It doesn't just tell you something failed: it groups the problem, shows the calls that prove it, and gives you the fix instructions to paste into your coding assistant.
features.ask: When a call goes wrong today, how long does it take your team to get from the complaint to a fix?
features.limits: Recommendations are suggestions; a human still decides and re-runs the suite.
features.ask_technical: Do your engineers already use a coding agent that could take these fix prompts directly?

features.name: Text Mode
features.does: Runs scenarios as text, skipping speech models, to test the LLM, tools and conversation logic fast and cheaply; requests run at low priority so they never take capacity from live calls.
features.value: Cheap enough to run on every code change, so regressions are caught in the change that caused them.
features.say: The fast mode checks the agent's thinking and actions as text, cheap enough to run on every change, and it never steals capacity from your live calls.
features.ask: How often does your team change prompts or tools: daily, weekly, or per release?
features.limits: Doesn't exercise speech recognition, turn-taking or interruptions.
features.ask_technical: Is your LLM on LiveKit Inference (low-priority scheduling applies) or your own provider keys?

features.name: Audio Mode and Degraded Callers
features.does: The simulated caller speaks over real audio, backchannels and interrupts; the run measures caller-heard latency (p50/p95/p99), turn-taking, transcription accuracy and can add background noise, a low-quality mic or packet loss.
features.value: Catches what only voice exposes, like the agent going silent, talking over people, or mishearing numbers on a bad line, before a customer does.
features.say: Voice mode makes the fake caller actually talk, with noise and a bad connection if you want, so you hear how your agent holds up in a parking lot, not just in a quiet office.
features.ask: Where are your callers usually calling from: quiet offices, cars, busy stores?
features.limits: Runs in real time, calls your STT/TTS on every turn and is metered higher than text; supported in ~50 languages.
features.ask_technical: Do you want --background-noise / --packet-loss runs in your nightly pipeline?

features.name: Turn into a Test (from a real call)
labels: Show me how to run it
features.does: Derives a scenario from a recorded session (or a run's scenario): a simulated user that reproduces the caller's goal and pass criteria for the judge, downloadable as scenario.yaml.
features.value: Every bad production call becomes a permanent regression test, so the same failure can't come back unnoticed.
features.say: Here's a real customer call. One click turns it into a repeatable test, with the caller's goal and what a good answer must include, so that mistake can never sneak back in.
features.ask: What's a call that went badly recently that you'd never want to happen again?
use_cases: Building a suite from production traffic
Validating a migration against real calls
features.limits: Needs a recorded session with Agent insights (30-day retention). Generation takes ~10-20 s. The derived scenario describes one call; generalize it before committing.
features.ask_technical: Where would the downloaded scenario.yaml live: next to the agent code in your repo?

features.name: CI Integration
features.does: Runs the committed scenarios.yaml in CI (e.g. GitHub Actions); the CLI exits non-zero when a scenario fails and prints a link to the run.
features.value: Agent quality is gated like any other code; broken behavior can't merge.
features.say: Drop the same tests into your build pipeline and a change that breaks a conversation fails the build, just like a broken unit test.
features.ask: Do you have a release process today where a quality check can block a change from going live?
features.limits: CI needs LIVEKIT_URL/API key/secret plus any provider keys the agent reads.
features.ask_technical: Which CI do you use, and can it hold LiveKit and model provider secrets?

features.name: Customer Proof: Serve AI
features.does: Serve AI validated a full agent rewrite (from a 600-edge Retell graph to one prompt on LiveKit) against ~100 real production calls with Agent Simulations.
features.value: 98% pass rate before cutover, migration in 1 week, 15% higher containment, $320K additional yearly customer savings.
features.say: Serve AI rebuilt their whole agent and proved it on a hundred real calls before switching anyone over: 98 percent pass rate, done in a week, and containment went up 15 percent.
features.ask: If you migrated or rewrote your agent, how would you prove to the business it's at least as good as today?
features.ask_technical: Would you replay production transcripts as scenarios to validate a migration?

demo_instructions:
1. Frame the problem: voice agents are tested on the happy path, but they fail on the long tail (noisy lines, people who give an account number in three pieces, people who try to break it), and calling your own agent by hand doesn't scale. Ask: 'Today, how do you find out a prompt change broke something that used to work?' (if technical: 'What runs before an agent change ships: unit tests, manual calls, nothing?')
2. Click 'Simulations' in the left sidebar. demo-tour has no runs yet, so own it: 'Runs start from the CLI or CI and land here.' Point at 'lk agent simulate -n 5': one command reads your agent's code, invents five realistic callers including edge cases, runs them in parallel and grades each one.
3. Explain how a run works in one breath: a simulated caller with a persona and goal, your real agent and tools, and a judge that grades the whole call pass/fail with a reason. Text mode is cheap enough for every change and never takes capacity from live calls; voice mode adds real audio, noise and packet loss for the nightly pass.
4. Describe what a run page shows (from the launch walkthrough): 'Simulated scenarios' with Passed/Failed and the judge's reason, 'Summary' with Quality scores (task completion, conciseness, conversation flow; voice adds turn-taking and transcript accuracy) and 'Issues detected' with 'Copy fix prompt' for your coding agent. Ask: 'What would a perfect call for your top use case have to include?'
5. Pivot to something live: click 'Sessions', widen 'Past 24 hours' to 'Past 7 days', and open RM_SDfdxKCCwvzq (the Nimbus support call).
6. Click 'Agent insights', then 'Turn into a test'. Wait the 10-20 seconds while it derives the scenario, then show the dialog: the 'Test name', the 'Simulated user' that replays the caller's goal, and the 'Pass criteria' (expand with its '+N more' button). Say: 'a bad call becomes a permanent regression test.' Ask: 'What's one call that went badly recently that you'd never want repeated?'
7. Click 'Cancel' (never Download in the demo). Explain the loop: download scenario.yaml, commit it with the agent, and CI fails the build if that behavior ever regresses.
8. Proof point: Serve AI rewrote their agent from a 600-edge Retell graph to one prompt and validated it on ~100 real calls: 98% pass rate before cutover, 1 week, +15% containment.
9. Close: 'Simulations is GA on every LiveKit Cloud project and free through October; your agent's own LLM and speech usage bill as normal.' Next step: pick 10 real calls for your top use case, turn them into tests, and run them against your agent this week.
